newsitem.title: USA: Supreme Court stays execution of convicted killer.
newsitem.headline: Supreme Court stays execution of convicted killer.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday refused to overturn a U.S. appeals court's decision to spare the life of convicted killer Thomas Thompson, but said it would hear arguments in the case in October.
"There'll be no execution tonight," a Supreme Court spokeswoman said on Monday evening, just hours before Thompson's scheduled execution at San Quentin State Prison in California.

In a surprise move, the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals decided on Sunday, less than 36 hours before the scheduled execution, to spare Thompson's life and reverse his rape conviction. The state of California immediately appealed to the Supreme Court to overturn the ruling.

The Supreme Court -- which had previously denied an appeal by Thompson -- did not throw out the 9th Circuit Court's ruling, but said it would review the merits of the case when it resumed work in October after a summer break, the spokeswoman said.

She said the Supreme Court would hear arguments about the appeals court's surprise decision to review the Thompson case again after an earlier decision to deny the convicted killer's appeal, as well as California's allegation that a "miscarriage of justice" occurred.

Thompson, 42, was convicted in 1983 of raping and murdering Ginger Fleischli, 20, two years earlier at his apartment in Laguna Beach in southern California, after an evening of drinking and smoking hashish. He has protested his innocence, saying he passed out after consensual sex with Fleischli.
